messages:
alice.m: Heads up — after last night's attribute-normalize job a cluster of service accounts still have elevated admin roles. Looks like LDAP 'department' -> 'dept' rename backfill ran, but SCIM bindings didn't reconcile. Anyone seen this pattern?
benji: Oof. Which path in the pipeline failed — mapping, delete, or pruner?
alice.m: Initial grep shows deleted group aliases didn't trigger role removals. Example: role_binding for 'service/backup-agent' still present though extGroup was removed.
carlos: Provisioner logs show a bunch of 409 conflicts and then tombstone ops skipped. Pasting excerpt:
```
provisioner-bot: ERROR 2026-03-19T23:01:12Z scim-sync: mapping mismatch: externalGroupId=null -> skip delete for role 'service-admin'
provisioner-bot: WARN 2026-03-19T23:01:13Z scim-pruner: failed to decrypt tombstone metadata: KMS.Decrypt access denied for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/xxxx
HTTP 409: conflict updating memberships for group ext-ldap-123
```
dana: That KMS.Decrypt denied is suspicious — we rotated the provisioner KMS key last week and tightened the key policy. If pruner can't read tombstones it will skip deletes. I ran `scimctl backfill --since=2026-03-19` and it surfaced ~120 orphaned role_bindings.
provisioner-bot: deploy log: job scim-pruner (rev 4f3b) exit=1; error=KMS.DecryptAccessDenied; retry_count=3
benji: Ok immediate mitigation: we should temporarily revoke admin roles from service/* principals until we fix the backfill. Also patch pruner so KMS failures are treated as soft-fail (log + enqueue) instead of skipping deletes entirely.
dana: I can run an emergency revoke script but need SRE approval. Command I’ll use (dry-run first):
```bash
./scripts/revoke-orphaned-admins.sh --pattern="service/*" --dry-run
# sample output:
# would revoke role: admin from principal service/backup-agent@redwood-infra
# would revoke role: admin from principal service/metrics-pusher@redwood-infra
```
carlos: Approved. Please run dry-run and paste results. If good, run without --dry-run.
alice.m: Also we need to roll back the KMS key policy change or add the provisioner principal to the new policy; current evidence points to that. Who touched key-policy last week?
dana: I edited the policy to remove broad `kms:Decrypt` to principals outside infra, trying to tighten access. I can revert to the previous policy for the provisioner key and then scope down incrementally.
benji: Two follow-ups: 1) Add richer audit fields to SCIM events (include KMS key id + provisioner job id + returned KMS errors) so we can triage without diving logs. 2) Add a canary run for attribute-normalize in shadow mode for 24h before full backfill.
alice.m: Agreed on both. I'll own the audit-schema change. Dana, can you do the KMS policy rollback and hotfix the pruner? Carlos please run the revoke script once we confirm dry-run.
provisioner-bot: Created incident IN-2026-1257 and attached logs: https://go/reports/IN-2026-1257 :eyes:
carlos: Dry-run output looks correct, no false positives. Proceeding to execute live revoke now.
alice.m: Thanks — once revoke is done, run the backfill again and monitor for lingering bindings. I'll prepare a short postmortem template and assign owners. Checklist: revoke done, KMS policy rollback, pruner hotfix (soft-fail + retry queue), audit-schema change, attr-normalize shadowing.
dana: Starting rollback now. Will report back when KMS Decrypt succeeds in pruner job.
benji: Also let's add an alert if more than 10 role_bindings are created for service/* in a 5m window — likely sign of drift or bad mapping.
alice.m: Good call. I'll open a follow-up ticket to add the alert.
provisioner-bot: IN-2026-1257 updated: owner=alice.m, sla=72h, linked_changes=[patch/scim-pruner-softfail, infra/kms-policy-rollback]
carlos: :thumbsup: revoke completed and verified. No production impact observed beyond expected perms drop.
alice.m: Closing loop here — continuing post-incident actions in IN-2026-1257. Thanks all. :fire:
